issue.title: Opening an editor URL with a stray % returns "Internal Server Error" instead of the app
issue.body:
I visited an editor address containing a lone or malformed percent sign, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:4317/d/50%` or `http://127.0.0.1:4317/d/%E0%A4%A`. The page shows a plain `Internal Server Error` (HTTP 500), and the server logs `URIError: URI malformed`. The API contract says every non-API path returns the web client's `index.html`. A well-formed path such as `/d/50%25` does return it.

Reproduction (server running on 4317):
```
curl -i -H "Host: 127.0.0.1:4317" http://127.0.0.1:4317/d/50%
```
Actual: `500 text/plain; charset=UTF-8 Internal Server Error`, and the server log shows `URIError: URI malformed at decodeURIComponent`.
Expected: `200 text/html` with the editor page.

expected.cause: The catch-all static route in createApp (src/server/app.ts) calls decodeURIComponent on the request path without handling the URIError it throws for malformed percent-encoding.

notes: {"origin": "M5 real use: a genuine defect found in ArchDrawer at this commit and reproduced; replayed, not filed", "proof": "tsx p5.mts -> 'GET /d/50%25 -> 200 text/html'; then 'URIError: URI malformed at decodeURIComponent (app.ts:345:18)' and 'GET /d/50% -> 500 text/plain; charset=UTF-8 Internal Server Error'; the same for '/d/%E0%A4%A'"}
